summary: 2-day install for A Creative Touch at Chelsea Square, NYC: greenery and willow branches on the building scaffolding (sidewalk-shed canopy over the entrance), meant to stay up a year. 3 JS people + Donna's team, 10am–3pm each day. Priced per day as she asked; NYC premium applied. Big flags on working on the scaffold and long-term liability.

logistics_notes: Montclair HQ; ~1 hr each way with tunnel traffic.
No dock: street/garage parking on W 20th St; carry ladders + tools.
Per day (as Donna asked): ~$2,582 per day all-in (labor $1,856.25 + base $300 + share of van/tolls/ladders + 8%).
No strike: the venue handles removal in a year.
reasoning: She asked for 3 people × 2 days, 10–3, and Donna's team of 3 works alongside: 6 people total is reasonable for a scaffold façade of this size.
Portal-to-portal 8.25 hrs/day (10–3 on site + NYC drive both ways + setup/cleanup).
NYC premium (+$10/hr): Manhattan street parking, no dock, carrying ladders + tools, sidewalk work.
Can't size from scope yet: no measurements or height. 3 × 2 days is her ask; confirm coverage area.
red_flags: WORKING ON SCAFFOLDING: who owns the scaffold, and are our people allowed on it? NYC may require scaffold-trained workers and the scaffold company's sign-off. If not allowed, ladders only (scaffold height unknown).

Long-term outdoor install (1 year) over a public sidewalk: falling branches/wire are a liability. Our scope is labor under Donna's direction; add a clause that JS isn't responsible for durability, maintenance or removal.
COI almost certainly required (NYC building + scaffold contractor), likely naming additional insureds.
Dates not locked (she hopes Nov 2–3; we're open Nov 3–6).
Budget: she declined the 10/24 Hamilton Farm quote for budget.
missing_info: Scaffold height + who owns it; are we allowed on it?
Square footage / linear feet of coverage
client_questions: Who owns the scaffolding, and will they allow our team to work on it?
Roughly how many feet of scaffolding are we covering?
Will the building need a COI from us?
client_history: Second inquiry from A Creative Touch this month; she declined the 10/24 Hamilton Farm quote for budget. Classic 'not budgeted for us yet' first-timer. Quote the real job and give her a lean option.
lean_option: Day 1 with 3 JS people to set the structure and hard-to-reach parts, Day 2 her team finishes with 1 JS lead: about $3,900 instead of $5,165.
